about: TribeCode marketplace: a curated, offline catalog of real things a tribe can add — sidebar widgets (links to real tools and built-in views), company templates, role playbooks (original TribeCode checklists), Claude Code skills, open-source libraries, tools and studios, site starters, MCP connectors, asset packs, legal templates (starting points, not legal advice) and academy tracks. GitHub repos were checked with git ls-remote and their license read from the LICENSE file on 2026-11-09; web addresses were checked by fetching them on 2026-11-09. "score" is TribeCode's own curated score (0-100), not a rating or download count. "added" is when the item joined TribeCode's catalog. Rankings like Hot and Rising come from what YOUR tribe uses (stored in your tribe folder), never from a central server.

items.title: Weekly CEO review
items.summary: Look back, pick next week’s one big thing, unblock seats.
steps: Read each seat’s last update and status
Check goals: what moved, what didn’t, and why
Pick ONE focus for next week and write it down
Clear anything marked “needs you” first
Post a short note to the crew with the focus

items.title: Your first 30 days
items.summary: From idea to a first paying (or playing) person.
steps: Write the mission in one sentence
Talk to 5 people who have the problem
Build the smallest thing that helps one of them
Put it in front of them and watch, don’t explain
Decide: keep, change or drop. Write why

items.title: Staff a seat with an agent
items.summary: Give an AI helper a seat with a clear charter.
steps: Pick the seat and write its goal for this month
List what it may do on its own
List what always needs a human approval
Set a weekly budget (0 is fine)
Review its first three updates closely

items.title: Ship safely
items.summary: A small checklist before anything reaches real users.
steps: Run the tests and look at the preview
Ask one person to try the change
Write what changed in plain words
Ship behind an approval for production
Watch errors for an hour after

items.title: Pick boring tech
items.summary: Choose tools the crew and agents can keep running.
steps: Prefer what the code already uses
Check the license and that it’s maintained
Write the choice in TOOLBOX.md with one reason
Avoid a second tool that does the same job
Revisit only when it really hurts

items.title: When something breaks
items.summary: Calm steps for outages and bad bugs.
steps: Say it out loud in chat: what’s broken, who’s on it
Roll back first if you can, fix second
Tell affected users what happened, simply
Write a short note: cause, fix, how to avoid
Add a test or a check for it

items.title: Brand basics
items.summary: Name, colors, type and voice in one page.
steps: Pick two or three colors and write their hex codes
Pick one font for headings, one for text
Write three words for how you sound
Make a simple logo or wordmark
Put it all in one doc the crew can find

items.title: Five-person usability test
items.summary: Watch real people use it and fix what trips them up.
steps: Write three tasks a new person should manage
Find five people (friends of friends is fine)
Watch them try, say little, take notes
List every stumble, worst first
Fix the top three and test again

items.title: Launch week
items.summary: Plan a calm, well-timed launch.
steps: Pick the launch day and the one place you’ll post first
Write the one-line pitch and a short demo clip
Line up 5 friends to try it on day one
Post, reply to every comment that day
Write down what brought people in

items.title: Start a newsletter
items.summary: Own your audience with a simple monthly email.
steps: Choose a tool (Buttondown, beehiiv or Kit)
Add a sign-up form to your site
Write the first issue: what you made and why
Send on the same day each month
Only email people who signed up

items.title: One number a week
items.summary: Track the single number that shows progress.
steps: Pick one number (sign-ups, players, revenue)
Write down where it is today
Check it the same day each week
Note one thing that might have moved it
Don’t make up or guess numbers

items.title: Your first ten customers
items.summary: Find and close the first ten by hand.
steps: List 30 people or companies with the problem
Reach out personally, not with a template blast
Offer a call to learn, not to pitch
Ask for the sale when it clearly helps them
Write down every “no” and its reason

items.title: Price check
items.summary: Test your price with real conversations.
steps: Write what you charge and what’s included
Ask five buyers what they’d expect to pay
Try one higher price with the next five
Keep it simple: one or two plans
This is not financial advice; check with a pro

items.title: Support inbox routine
items.summary: Answer fast, kindly, and learn from every ticket.
steps: Check the inbox twice a day at set times
Reply within a day, even if just “on it”
Tag each ticket: bug, question, idea
Turn repeated questions into a help page
Share the top three themes with the crew weekly

items.title: Write a help center
items.summary: Ten short answers that save everyone time.
steps: List the ten questions people ask most
Answer each in under 150 words
Add a screenshot where it helps
Link it from the app and your emails
Review it every month

items.title: Weekly rhythm
items.summary: A light routine so nothing falls through.
steps: Monday: plan the week in the daily plan
Midweek: quick standup in chat
Friday: demo what got done
Keep a running list of decisions
Archive what’s finished

items.title: Tool audit
items.summary: Keep the stack small and paid-for things in check.
steps: List every tool and who uses it
Mark each: must have, nice to have, unused
Cancel or remove the unused
Write who owns each remaining tool
Repeat every quarter

items.title: Monthly money check
items.summary: Know what came in, what went out, and what’s left.
steps: Export income and costs for the month
Sort costs into a few simple groups
Compare to last month
Note your runway in months
Starting point only, not financial advice; ask an accountant

items.title: Set a simple budget
items.summary: Agree what the crew may spend and on what.
steps: Write a monthly limit for the whole project
Set a weekly limit for each seat (0 is fine)
Anything above a limit needs an approval
Review spending at the monthly check
Check local tax rules with a professional

items.title: Legal basics checklist
items.summary: The paperwork most small projects need.
steps: Agree who owns what (a cofounder or IP agreement)
Have a privacy policy if you collect any personal data
Use terms of service for a public product
Use an NDA or contractor agreement when hiring help
Templates are a starting point, not legal advice; check local law

items.title: Check licenses
items.summary: Make sure everything you use may be used.
steps: List libraries, art and sounds you use
Check each license (MIT, Apache, CC0 are easy)
Keep credits in CREDITS.md
Avoid share-alike licenses in things you sell, unless you mean to
Ask a lawyer when money or doubt is involved
